status: Separate post-discovery critical review; not part of arm U generation or its search budget
original_arm_integrity: U.json was not opened, edited or rewritten during this review. Findings here must not be attributed retrospectively to the original discovery run.

task.proposed_arrangement: Several employers jointly revise consenting employees' permitted roster options while preserving production coverage, and commit the resulting childcare demand to a provider through conditional minimum demand, notice and finite fallback obligations.
task.objective: Look for complete equivalent offerings and obvious overlaps; identify only the gap supported by the retrieved evidence.
task.external_actions: Public reading only. No contact, contract, operational action, transaction or legal advice.

verdict.broad_novelty_claim: Not supportable. Employer consortia, flexible reserved care, worker-involved roster changes, reservation funding and limited backup arrangements are established components.
verdict.narrow_remaining_claim: A coupled commissioning instrument could make employer roster choices, individual worker consent, provider capacity and contingent funding/notice/fallback terms mutually consistent in a specified case.
verdict.exact_supported_gap: The retrieved public sources do not document a single available service that performs the whole conjunction. In particular, none demonstrates joint revision of multiple participating employers' production-preserving rosters together with the resulting provider minimum-demand/notice/fallback commitments. This is a documentation gap in a bounded search, not proof of an unmet market or absence of equivalent private arrangements.
verdict.worthwhile_to_construct: Conditionally yes, as a small falsifiable feasibility construction. This probe alone does not justify selecting it as a novel flagship.
verdict.confidence: High that the broad ingredients have strong prior art; low-to-moderate that a commercially important integration gap remains.
verdict.novelty_ceiling: Do not claim external novelty validation. A distinct-combination score of 2 would require a clearer documented transaction gap and a competent existing-provider/manual-coordination comparator; a familiar-implementation score of 1 remains plausible.

equivalence_definition.rule: A complete equivalent must jointly deliver the following functions in one arrangement; a combination of ordinary services also counts if it can be commissioned without the proposed instrument.

features.meaning: Multiple independent employers participate in the same care-capacity arrangement.
The arrangement changes the employers' work rosters, rather than merely adapting care to already determined shifts.
Specified operational coverage and useful output remain satisfied.
Individual employees' permitted shift/care choices and consent are explicit constraints.
A provider receives an explicit conditional minimum quantity or payment commitment with a notice/freeze rule.
Withdrawal, disruption and fallback obligations are finite, allocated and financially feasible.

equivalence_definition.interpretation: Marketing silence is coded as not documented, not as a claim that a supplier cannot provide a feature. Customized conventional contracting can falsify the novelty claim even if no supplier uses the proposed product label.

sources.title: WorkFamily Solutions FAQ
sources.organization: WorkFamily Solutions, a Kindergarden and Bright Horizons initiative
sources.evidence: An employer reserves annual places; care can vary with employee shifts and a place can serve different children. Parents manage preferences and agree to offers. Flexible care is restricted to regular weekday opening hours.
sources.limits: No full commercial contract was examined. Multi-employer roster redesign and contingent notice/fallback terms are not documented.

sources.title: Child Care Cooperatives
sources.organization: North Dakota Association of Rural Electric Cooperatives
sources.access: Facilitator's own cooperative-model description, opened successfully
sources.evidence: Employer members can jointly support childcare and contract with an established center or licensed home network. Parent/employee governance can be combined with the employer model.
sources.strength: Strong prior art for the organizational form, although not a verified complete commercial offering.
sources.limits: No jointly computed employer rosters, minimum-demand contract or individual consent protocol is specified.

sources.title: Employee and union developed shift schedules, Letter of Understanding 26
sources.organization: Covenant Health and Health Sciences Association of Alberta
sources.access: Agreement published by a contracting party, opened successfully
sources.evidence: Employee/union-designed schedules must meet operational requirements and avoid extra costs. At least 75 percent of affected employees must agree before implementation.
sources.strength: Primary evidence that worker-involved roster redesign with operational constraints is established.
sources.limits: This is a single-employer agreement without childcare commissioning. Collective approval is not the same as the proposed individual opt-in constraint. No legal conclusion is drawn.

sources.title: Supporting Working Parents: Solutions to Childcare Barriers in the Skilled Trades
sources.organization: Building Trades of Alberta with Build Together
sources.access: Original stakeholder report; PDF opened and relevant sections located
sources.observed_date: PDF states last revised February 15, 2023; URL upload directory is June 2024
sources.evidence: The report proposes later starting shifts, flexible schedules, job sharing and childcare support. Its later-start example may preserve a full day where possible, or reduce hours if later work is unavailable. It also describes notice and limited relief obligations in job-sharing examples.
sources.strength: Strong adverse prior art for changing work schedules around care rather than assuming work schedules are fixed.
sources.limits: Recommendations and examples do not demonstrate a jointly contracted multi-employer/provider service or preservation of every original production requirement.

sources.title: Child Care and the Private Sector: Profitability and Prosperity
sources.organization: Employer-supported childcare roadmap; publisher identity was not independently verified from the retrieved excerpt
sources.access: Guide PDF opened; reservation and consortium sections located
sources.evidence: The guide describes multi-employer provider contracts, prepaid reservations with possible unused-slot refunds, and bounded backup-care benefits. It points to KinderCare and Learning Care Group as suppliers.
sources.strength: Corroborating prior-art guide, not independently verified supplier contract evidence.
sources.limits: Do not treat its example benefit limits or attributed current supplier features as verified contract terms. The attempted primary KinderCare open failed.

sources.title: KinderCare employer-sponsored childcare page
sources.limits: No inference about absent services or capabilities follows from the access failure.

sources.title: Our Promise — childcare pilot
sources.access: Substantive search excerpt from the sponsor's own page; not separately opened
sources.evidence: Horizon describes dedicated childcare places, including flex-time spaces, provided through local childcare operators for staff and physicians.
sources.strength: Primary sponsor description of a concrete shift-work-oriented care program.
sources.limits: No evidence of multi-employer roster co-design or the complete proposed commitments.

obvious_overlaps.assessment: Direct provider overlap; cannot be the novelty headline.

main_falsifier.statement: An existing provider, consortium facilitator or ordinary competent coordinator can already assemble the same consenting worker options, production coverage, provider commitments and finite contingencies through its standard or custom contracts at comparable all-in cost.
main_falsifier.why_strong: The evidence already contains almost all the components. Lack of a single marketing page describing their conjunction is weak novelty evidence.
main_falsifier.what_would_count: A public operating manual, a documented deployment, or an authorized example agreement/workflow showing the whole conjunction. A practical equivalent assembled from existing services also counts.
main_falsifier.what_does_not_count: Merely changing the name, using a solver instead of a spreadsheet, matching care to fixed rosters, promising unlimited backup, ignoring staff coverage, or making workers accept schedules outside their stated options.

narrower_construction_test.claim_to_test: For a specified cohort, construct a jointly acceptable roster-and-care commitment package that turns an infeasible or unfunded initial arrangement into a feasible funded one without relaxing useful output, worker choices or provider constraints.
narrower_construction_test.minimal_artifact: An explicit option table, production-coverage constraints, childcare capacity/age/staffing constraints, consent requirements, demand/payment floor, notice deadline and a finite contingency table with payer obligations.
necessary_counterfactuals: Existing flexible reserved care with the initial work schedules.
A competent ordinary consortium plus employer-led scheduling and existing provider contracts, with the same information and freedom to coordinate.
The proposed coupled instrument, with all coordination, reserve and fallback costs charged.
narrower_construction_test.decision_rule: Proceed only if the construction exposes a real additional acceptable arrangement or a concrete missing commitment. If the ordinary coordinated alternative reaches the same result, report a useful implementation rather than a newly enabled mechanism.
decisive_failures: Demand concentration arises only by forcing a worker outside their permitted choices or reducing their promised hours without consent.
Production is reduced, skill coverage disappears, or the childcare provider's feasible capacity is exceeded.
A minimum payment is supported only by expected parent attendance rather than an identified funded payer.
The apparent surplus disappears after reserve staffing, unused seats, administration and finite fallback costs.
Benefits depend on treating an unverified provider marketing promise as an enforceable, unlimited guarantee.
narrower_construction_test.claim_boundaries: A synthetic feasible construction would establish only the modeled result. Real willingness to change shifts, provider acceptance, enforceability, source rights and demand require separate evidence. No such evidence was obtained in this review.

scope_limitations: Four queries and six page-open attempts are not a complete supplier, contractual, patent or research review.
Full reservation contracts were not available in the examined sources.
A key primary supplier page returned 403; this weakens a negative finding.
Some results concerned childcare providers' own educator rosters, which were excluded because they do not demonstrate employers redesigning parents' work shifts.
No provider or employer was contacted, and no private contracting practices were inferred.
Search-result publication-age labels were not treated as reliable dates where a document supplied its own revision date.
